notes: Powers /pick-stack/. Each answer carries weights that bias the recommendation toward one of the named stacks below. The PickStack island sums weights across answers and recommends the highest-scoring stack, then shows 'why not the alternatives' from loser_rationale.

schema.questions[].id: stable slug — used in the share-URL hash
schema.questions[].options[].label: user-facing option label
schema.questions[].options[].weights: object — stack name -> integer weight (positive = favor, negative = disfavor)
schema.stacks[].name: display name
schema.stacks[].loser_rationale: object — losing stack name -> short why-not

questions.prompt: Hard real-time latency need (does p50 < 500ms matter)?

options.label: No, agent loops are async / background

questions.prompt: How strong does code-execution isolation need to be?

options.label: Dev loop on engineer's machine — host is fine

questions.prompt: Primary language for the agent runtime?

options.label: Pay for best — under $5 / PR is fine

questions.prompt: How important is first-class MCP tool support?

options.label: Must-have — agents will call many MCP servers

questions.prompt: Sync (chat / IDE) or async (background PR fleet)?

options.label: Sync — interactive, in an IDE or chat
Async — durable background fleet opening PRs

questions.prompt: License preference for the stack itself?

options.label: OSS only — must self-host the pieces I care about
Mixed — OSS where it helps, proprietary where it ships faster
Proprietary fine — I want vendor support

questions.prompt: How serious is the observability story?

options.label: Critical — production traces, evals, SLO alerts
Just enough — logs + a tracing UI

stacks.name: anthropic-prod

components.inference: Anthropic API (Claude Sonnet for impl, Haiku for routing)
components.harness: Claude Code or Claude Agent SDK

stacks.rationale: If the agent ships PRs and you want the best coding model in the loop, this stack pays the premium where it matters (inference) and stays OSS everywhere else.

loser_rationale.openai-prod: GPT-class models lag Sonnet on agentic coding eval suites by ~10 points on SWE-bench Verified at time of writing — pick this stack instead if Sonnet is available.
loser_rationale.groq-fast: Groq is excellent for low-latency but does not host Claude. Use it for routing, not the implementation step.
loser_rationale.cerebras-fast: Same caveat as Groq — open-weight throughput leader, but not where you want your final code-writing call.
loser_rationale.nebius-oss: If cost dominates and SWE-bench-grade results matter less than throughput, Nebius wins on dollars per million tokens.
loser_rationale.together-oss: Together is the cheaper Llama path; pick it when you have post-trained your own coding model.
loser_rationale.self-hosted-vllm: Self-hosting Sonnet is impossible (proprietary weights). vLLM only competes once you commit to open weights.
loser_rationale.vercel-edge: Vercel's edge stack is best when the agent UI runs in a browser session, not when it runs as a long background PR fleet.

stacks.name: openai-prod

components.inference: OpenAI API (GPT-5 for impl, 4.1-mini for routing)

stacks.rationale: First-party OpenAI loop with Agents SDK + Codex — strongest single-vendor story when your team already standardizes on OpenAI and wants tracing + evals in one place.

loser_rationale.anthropic-prod: If your benchmark numbers favor Claude on the workload you actually care about, the Anthropic stack wins on raw code quality.
loser_rationale.groq-fast: Use Groq alongside, not instead — route classification tasks to Groq, keep implementation on GPT.
loser_rationale.cerebras-fast: Same as Groq — throughput leader, but you still want a top-tier model for the implementation step.
loser_rationale.nebius-oss: Cheaper per token, weaker on first-party tooling — pick when cost matters more than vendor support.
loser_rationale.together-oss: Pick when you've fine-tuned your own model — otherwise OpenAI's tooling is more polished.
loser_rationale.self-hosted-vllm: Operational burden is large; only worth it at thousands of QPS or with a regulatory mandate.
loser_rationale.vercel-edge: Vercel is great for the UI tier; pair them rather than choose between them.

stacks.name: groq-fast
stacks.rationale: Sub-500ms p50 across the entire loop — Groq's LPUs hold the latency floor in the field, and Llama is good enough for most non-frontier work.

loser_rationale.anthropic-prod: Sonnet beats Llama on code quality but adds ~3-5x latency under load — pick Anthropic when quality dominates.
loser_rationale.openai-prod: Same trade — GPT is higher quality, higher latency.
loser_rationale.cerebras-fast: Cerebras and Groq compete on the same axis; pick by which models they host (Cerebras leads on Qwen Coder, Groq on Llama).
loser_rationale.nebius-oss: Nebius wins on cost per million tokens; Groq wins on tokens per second.
loser_rationale.together-oss: Together hosts more models with more SKUs; Groq hosts fewer but faster.
loser_rationale.self-hosted-vllm: Self-hosted vLLM can match Groq's quality but not its latency without custom hardware.
loser_rationale.vercel-edge: Vercel is the UI layer, not the inference layer — pair them.

stacks.name: cerebras-fast

components.inference: Cerebras (Qwen Coder for impl, Llama for routing)

stacks.rationale: Massive throughput per dollar with state-of-the-art open coding models — pick this when you're running thousands of evals in parallel.

loser_rationale.anthropic-prod: Claude has the quality edge but you'll wait minutes for parallel runs that finish in seconds on Cerebras.
loser_rationale.openai-prod: Same as above — better single-call quality, worse parallel economics.
loser_rationale.groq-fast: Groq leads on single-call latency; Cerebras leads on aggregate throughput.
loser_rationale.nebius-oss: Nebius is more general-purpose (you can also run training jobs); Cerebras is inference-only.
loser_rationale.together-oss: Together is the cheaper backstop; Cerebras the faster primary.
loser_rationale.self-hosted-vllm: vLLM on commodity GPUs caps out at a fraction of Cerebras throughput per dollar.
loser_rationale.vercel-edge: Different layer — Cerebras for the model, Vercel for the UI.

stacks.name: nebius-oss
stacks.rationale: Pennies per million tokens, EU data residency, and Contree's branching sandbox for tree-of-thought workflows — the best stack when cost and reproducibility both matter.

loser_rationale.anthropic-prod: Anthropic wins on raw quality and MCP polish; lose if your budget is constrained or you need EU residency.
loser_rationale.openai-prod: Same as above; OpenAI also has stronger first-party tracing.
loser_rationale.groq-fast: Groq wins on single-call latency; Nebius wins on cost per million tokens.
loser_rationale.cerebras-fast: Cerebras wins on raw throughput; Nebius wins on stack breadth (storage, K8s, GPUs).
loser_rationale.together-oss: Together is the closer competitor — pick Nebius when you also want managed Kubernetes and GPU rental in the same account.
loser_rationale.self-hosted-vllm: Self-hosting beats Nebius on cost at very high scale; Nebius wins on operational simplicity.

stacks.name: together-oss
stacks.rationale: If you've post-trained your own coding model and want serverless + dedicated endpoint options in one vendor, Together is the cleanest landing spot.

loser_rationale.anthropic-prod: Anthropic wins on out-of-the-box quality without training; Together wins on customization.
loser_rationale.openai-prod: OpenAI offers fine-tuning too, but Together is cheaper and supports more open models.
loser_rationale.groq-fast: Groq is faster per call; Together hosts more model SKUs.
loser_rationale.cerebras-fast: Cerebras hosts fewer models; pick Together for catalog breadth.
loser_rationale.nebius-oss: Very close call — Nebius edges on cost and GPU rental, Together on fine-tune ergonomics.
loser_rationale.self-hosted-vllm: Self-host when scale demands it; otherwise Together's managed endpoints save weeks.

stacks.name: self-hosted-vllm

components.inference: vLLM on your own GPUs (Llama / DeepSeek / Qwen Coder)

stacks.rationale: Everything OSS, everything on your hardware — pick this when regulation, data residency, or air-gapped deployment is the binding constraint.

loser_rationale.anthropic-prod: Anthropic is impossible to self-host (proprietary weights); only viable if you can route to an API.
loser_rationale.groq-fast: Groq's latency advantage comes from custom silicon you cannot replicate on commodity GPUs.
loser_rationale.cerebras-fast: Same as Groq — proprietary wafer-scale hardware.
loser_rationale.nebius-oss: Nebius lets you start with managed inference and graduate to your own GPU clusters in the same account — softer landing than full self-host.
loser_rationale.together-oss: Together's managed endpoints save weeks of operational pain; self-host only if regulation forces it.

stacks.name: vercel-edge

components.inference: Vercel AI Gateway (routing across Anthropic / OpenAI / Groq)

stacks.rationale: If your front end already runs on Vercel and your agents need to talk to it, this stack ships in days — every primitive is TypeScript-first and edge-native.

loser_rationale.anthropic-prod: Pure Anthropic stack wins for Python shops; Vercel wins for Next.js shops.
loser_rationale.groq-fast: Vercel's gateway can route to Groq — you can have both.
loser_rationale.nebius-oss: Nebius is a sovereign-cloud play; Vercel is a developer-velocity play.
loser_rationale.together-oss: Vercel's gateway can hit Together; the choice is at the UI/runtime layer.
loser_rationale.self-hosted-vllm: Different posture entirely — Vercel is fully managed.
